matched_rules.because: Two cooling systems in one data center failed simultaneously while outside temperatures were extraordinarily high, matching the rule's conditions for treating redundant cooling failure as a single-point-of-failure event.
With mechanical cooling affected and no confirmation yet that it is running, the site must be treated as running on a load-dependent thermal buffer and action taken before automated shutdowns begin.
Cooling capacity is in question and temperatures are at risk of exceeding safe operating thresholds, so progressive thermal load reduction should be considered before full shutdown.
Multiple cooling systems are affected and manual intervention may be required, so extra technicians should be staged before attempting manual restarts.

next_actions.action: Immediately verify whether mechanical cooling systems are still running and assess whether the data center can maintain a safe operating temperature; if not, plan to power down servers to prevent a longer outage or damage.
Treat the thermal buffer as finite and act before it is depleted; expect automated device shutdown once safe thresholds are exceeded.
Progressively decrease thermal load, considering termination of non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs, before resorting to full server shutdown.
Increase technician staffing at the datacenter so manual restart procedures can be executed promptly and in parallel across data halls.

escalate.reason: Simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems combined with extraordinarily high outside temperatures means the data center may be unable to maintain a safe operating temperature, and thermal buffer depletion or automated shutdowns may be imminent.

not_covered: No rule addresses the specific cause of the cooling-system issue (e.g., water/air ingress, chiller cluster binding, or control-system failover) because the first-hour signals do not yet identify the failure mechanism.
No rule covers the initial alerting and investigation workflow itself; the pill assumes cooling loss is already confirmed or strongly suspected.
No rule addresses coordination with the utility provider or storm-related power quality beyond the voltage-swell scenario in R-001, which is not yet evidenced in the signals.

per_finding.note: R-005 explicitly matches simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems combined with extraordinarily high outside temperatures.
R-006 directs progressively decreasing thermal load, including termination of non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs.
R-005's next action includes planning to power down servers to prevent a longer outage or damage.
R-006 already applies the practice of progressively decreasing thermal load before full shutdown.
No rule addresses auditing cooling system equipment and standards across data centers.
No rule covers measuring or reporting the total duration of the cooling system failure impact.
